clue.text: Head of Manchester University board is not fixed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Manchester is used

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging or a boardroom table

explanation.surface: A university's governing board is said to be fickle, starting with its Manchester head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutable is changeable, liable to alter rather than staying settled.

clue.text: Make fun of riding in experimental model

parts.note: to mock is to make fun of
a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone teases another rider inside a prototype.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-up is a full-size trial version of something, built to test a design.

clue.text: Part of car made of gold supporting heavy weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: a tonne is a heavy metric weight
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A car component made of gold has to bear a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts AU below TONNE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is the rear passenger section of an open car, or its cover.

clue.text: Cover the eyes and collapse after drinking bout

indicators.note: after says the collapse word comes following the drinking word

parts.note: a blind is old British slang for a drinking spree
a business that folds collapses

explanation.surface: Someone shades their eyes and keels over after a heavy session.
explanation.definitionFit: A blindfold is a bandage tied over a person's eyes, and to apply one is to block their sight.

clue.text: Sort of church to get confirmed in

definitions.meaning: a state-recognised church such as the Church of England is the official national one
someone confirmed in a post is settled securely in it

explanation.surface: A kind of church where you go to be confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Church of England is the official state church; and someone made secure in office has become settled there.

clue.text: For example, Rosemary's carry-on with bishop

parts.note: a carry-on is a fuss or commotion, a pother
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A woman called Rosemary is making a fuss alongside a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosemary looks like a woman's name, but it is the herb; the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a culinary herb grown in the kitchen garden, an example of a leafy plant for the pot.

clue.text: Remove shells from part of aircraft

definitions.meaning: to shell peas or beans is to take them from their husks
a streamlined housing under a wing, holding an engine or fuel

explanation.surface: Take the cartridges out of a section of a warplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelling peas means taking them from their husks; and an engine nacelle on a plane is also called this.

clue.text: Like the rise and fall of a sound

definitions.text: Like the rise and fall of a sound

parts.words: Like the rise and fall of a sound
parts.note: seems to describe a noise getting louder and softer, but the sound is a sea inlet whose water level goes up and down

explanation.surface: A noise swelling and fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea, as in a coastal inlet.

clue.text: The language of the American side!

definitions.meaning: the tongue spoken in Britain and the US
in American billiards and pool, side or spin put on the cue ball is called by this name

explanation.surface: The way the Americans talk!
explanation.walkthrough: In US pool, spin on the ball is called 'English'; the British call it side.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the tongue of England; and Americans use the same word for spin imparted to a cue ball.

clue.text: Bigmouth is first to gamble in card game requiring skill

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the run of the game and the skill

parts.note: brag is a British card game similar to poker
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of gamble is used

explanation.surface: A loudmouth is the first to bet in a card game that needs talent.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAG is a British card game like poker; 'requiring' simply joins the game to the skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a boaster, someone who talks big about themselves.

clue.text: Cheating by little boys condemned

parts.note: a con is a swindle, an act of cheating
Vic is a short form of the boy's name Victor
Ted is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: Some young lads have been found guilty of cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little boys' is one phrase supplying two pet names in a row; 'by' merely joins the cheating to them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be convicted is to be found guilty in court, the judgement that leaves a person condemned.

clue.text: It sounds like knife is needed for Indian hemp

indicators.note: the clue openly says we want a word pronounced like the next one, not spelt like it

parts.note: a dagger is a short stabbing knife

explanation.surface: A blade is apparently required to deal with a cannabis plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent DAGGER and DAGGA are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagga is the South African name for cannabis, the plant also called Indian hemp.

clue.text: Overturn report written by union leader

indicators.note: a leader is the front runner, so only the opening letter of union is wanted
a report is something heard, so the word for written is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: something written has been penned

explanation.surface: A trade union boss writes up a report calling for things to be turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places U beside the second piece; PEND is said like 'penned'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to tip it over so its base is on top, to overturn it.

clue.text: An inclination for the square cut

definitions.text: An inclination for the square cut

parts.words: An inclination for the square cut
parts.note: reads like a batsman's fondness for the cricket stroke, but describes cutting a slope onto a right-angled edge

explanation.surface: A cricketer has a liking for playing the square cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The square cut is a cricket shot played square of the wicket; here the square is a right-angled edge being cut to an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a sloping edge where a square one was gives a slanted surface, an inclination away from the right angle.

clue.text: Unsettled existence in southern states associated with slavery

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a southern US state
GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, another southern US state
bondage is slavery or servitude

explanation.surface: A rootless life in the Deep South, tied up with the history of slavery.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagabondage is the condition of a vagrant, a wandering life without a fixed home.

clue.text: One who lays down his own life for others

definitions.text: One who lays down his own life for others

parts.words: One who lays down his own life for others
parts.note: sounds like a self-sacrificing martyr, but laying down a life here means setting it down in writing for readers

explanation.surface: A hero gives up his life so that other people may live.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of a memoir sets down the story of their own life for other people to read.

clue.text: A mother's story announced in the Economist

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; with the possessive it gives dam's

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the story word counts by its pronunciation

parts.note: a myth is a traditional story

explanation.surface: A mother's tale is reported in a financial weekly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Economist' looks like the magazine, but it is the 18th-century Scottish economist; MITH is said like 'myth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish thinker who wrote The Wealth of Nations is known as the father of modern economics.

clue.text: Artist's impressions about getting absorbed in oriental affairs

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction

indicators.note: getting absorbed in means the small word for about is soaked up inside the others

parts.note: affairs are things, matters to deal with
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An artist's sketches about being caught up in Eastern business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting absorbed in' puts C (circa) inside E + THINGS, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints taken from engraved plates, the impressions an artist pulls on paper.

clue.text: Theatre bars odd variety act

indicators.note: variety means a mixed assortment, so the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A theatre turns away a strange music-hall turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like the music hall, but it signals the anagram of THEATRE BARS ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is an idiom for performing on stage, that is, to act.

clue.text: Sound made by you to fake harmony

indicators.note: says the following word counts only for how it is pronounced

parts.note: the word you as it is pronounced
phony, or phoney, means fake

explanation.surface: The noise you make when pretending to be in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening EU of the answer is pronounced 'you'; 'to' merely joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is pleasantness of sound, sweet agreement of tones, much like harmony.

clue.text: Harsh treatment given to triads caught

indicators.note: treatment means the word triads gets worked over, its letters rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Caught gang members from Chinese triads are dealt with severely.
explanation.walkthrough: Triads are Chinese criminal gangs; 'treatment given to' signals their letters being reworked before the cricket C is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and severe, as harsh as can be.

clue.text: A photo with a lion's head at the top

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word lion

explanation.surface: A snapshot showing a lion's head up top.
explanation.definitionFit: Apical means relating to an apex, the tip or summit of something.

clue.text: Possible danger on short flight — it helps make us bitter

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another follows it, so the shuffled danger comes after the short flight

parts.note: a hop is a short trip by plane

indicators.note: possible means one potential version, so the letters of danger may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A brief plane trip might carry some risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' is English beer flavoured with hops, which a hop garden grows; 'us' is the plural of the bitter beer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop garden is a field where hops are cultivated, the crop that gives beer its bitterness.

clue.text: Representative for a cause

definitions.meaning: someone acting on behalf of another person
something that brings about an effect, as a chemical that produces a reaction

explanation.surface: A spokesperson for a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep acting for a principal has this title; so does any force that produces a result.

clue.text: Frank character

definitions.meaning: to frank a letter is to mark it as postage paid
a person's ... is their distinctive character or nature

explanation.surface: A candid personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Franking a letter marks it with postage, and a mark of nature or kind is also called this.

clue.text: Marriage bouquet, with extra love

indicators.note: with extra says another letter is slipped into the word for bouquet

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose, its smell
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A wedding bouquet comes with a little more affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Marriage as a noose is a jocular image of being tied down.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetiously, wedlock is pictured as a snare or loop that ties a person, hence a halter.

clue.text: Reverting to type. Hindu deity is put back in top place

indicators.note: in says the turned name goes within the word for the top place

parts.note: an attic is the room at the top of a house

indicators.note: put back means the deity's name is turned round and read from right to left

parts.note: Siva, also Shiva, is the Hindu god of destruction

explanation.surface: A Hindu god's statue is restored to its high place, which is a return to tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: Siva is also spelt Shiva; 'put back' turns the god round, and 'in' lodges the result within the attic. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavistic traits are throwbacks that recur from remote ancestors, a return to an earlier form.

clue.text: Sort of bed that is warm and dry

definitions.meaning: to put washing somewhere warm until fully dry

explanation.surface: A bed that is cosy and not damp.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress is so called; and laundry hung up somewhere warm to finish drying is being aired.

clue.text: Dubious lawyer taken in by mass hysteria

indicators.note: taken in by means the wanted word is held within the run of letters in mass hysteria

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer is fooled by public panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like deceived, but it signals letters held inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a disreputable, unscrupulous attorney.

clue.text: Others, too, round here in Rome, being honest

indicators.note: round says the word for others goes around the Latin word for here

parts.note: et al, Latin for and others, adds further people too
hic is Latin for here, the language of Rome

explanation.surface: Other people too, round here in Rome, are being truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ethical means acting with moral principle, being upright and truthful.
